evidence.note: Establishes an fp32 PyTorch reference implementation (baseline 133.6ms), which serves as the implicit correctness oracle for later comparisons.

Compares dtype choices (BF16/FP16/TF32) against fp32 at the exact rtol=atol=2e-2 gate; reports concrete max-abs-errors (0.0238) and rejects options that violate tolerance — genuine tolerance-gated verification on normal inputs.

Explicitly stress-tests the fragile heavy-tailed Cauchy distribution across scale factors (S=128/512), measuring errors (0.1175) and finding a stable scaling — targeted numerical-error reasoning on the known-hard case.
Full assembled-kernel check is only on one tiny shape [1,32,32,128] ('max diff of exactly 0.0'); no sweep over large N, high dim, or B variants of the complete kernel.
Mask/nomask handling is reasoned about but not clearly verified numerically against the reference — the masked path lacks an oracle comparison.
FP8 rejected on accuracy (max abs err 1.7); shows ongoing precision-vs-tolerance checking, but still component/dtype-focused rather than a domain-wide kernel harness.

reasoning: The agent maintains an fp32 reference and repeatedly gates dtype/scaling decisions against the exact 2e-2 tolerance, and notably stress-tests the fragile Cauchy case across scale factors — clearly beyond the level-3 'one tiny shape/one distribution' anchor. But the verification is concentrated on isolated components (bmm, producers) and dtype precision; the full assembled kernel is only checked on a single 32x32 shape, with no systematic sweep over N up to 2048, dim up to 768, B variants, or a clear masked-vs-reference comparison. This falls short of level 5's requirement of checking the kernel across several representative shapes including a masked case, placing it at a 4.
